baselines.note: newest pre-versioning release; an absent `version` field reads as 0. Legacy semantics: a string that cannot be parsed as a timestamp collapses to epoch (1970-01-01)
stricter timestamp parsing: an unparseable string stays a string instead of collapsing to epoch, failing fast rather than corrupting data
consistent MySQL timezone handling: binlog CDC uses TimestampStringLocation to match the connection's timezone, so CDC timestamps agree with Full Refresh
MySQL offset-format timezones (session or global) parse correctly and set the connection timezone instead of falling back to UTC
MySQL unsigned int/integer/bigint map to Int64; earlier they mapped to Int32 and overflowed

MongoDB BSON DateTime at any depth decodes to UTC time.Time via a custom client registry, preventing json.Marshal crashes for out-of-range years ([0,9999]); top-level DateTimes that previously formatted with the local machine timezone (e.g. "+05:30") now always output UTC ("Z")
ReformatInt64 accepts []uint8: numeric values some SQL drivers return as byte slices parse to int64 instead of erroring

parquet INT96 maps to Timestamp (the raw 96-bit value was emitted as a string, which disagreed with the inferred Timestamp schema and collapsed the column to String) and unsigned 32-bit widens to Int64, matching pg/mysql (earlier read as signed int32 and mapped to Int32, so values above 2^31-1 wrapped negative); older state keeps both previous behaviors so existing destination columns do not change type on upgrade
